userStories.title: Route input parsing and the gate-secret label
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add shared composite route-input parsing and separate the six secret-bearing routes from the high-risk rollout.

**Motivation** — Every other approvable write route is listed in `PENDING_GATE_ROUTES` with the feature that will gate it.

**Approach** — **`parseRouteInput` for composite id inputs.** `parseRouteInput(input, names)` (in `approvals/route/parse-route-input.ts`) answers an object with exactly the named members, each a non-empty string. A non-object input, an array, or a missing, empty or non-string member throws `ValidationAppException({}, 'approvals.invalidInput')`. The 5a helper `parseIdInput` stays where it is; new commands use `parseRouteInput(input, ['id'])`.

**`gate-secret` is chosen from an explicit list, not derived.** `SECRET_GATE_ROUTES` (exported from `pending-gate-routes.ts`) names the 6 labels. The integration rule checks that list first, so every other route keeps the 5a derivation.

- US-001:
  - `PendingGateFeature` becomes `'gate-high' | 'gate-secret' | 'gate-core-domains' | 'gate-fleet'`, and `isPendingGateFeature` accepts `gate-secret`;
  - the 6 secret-bearing rows are relabelled `gate-secret`;
  - `SECRET_GATE_ROUTES` holds exactly those 6 labels.
- The rollout rule (in `permission-contract.integration.spec.ts`), first match wins:
  1. a label in `SECRET_GATE_ROUTES` → `gate-secret`;
  2. a key whose default is not `none` → `gate-high`;
  3. all keys under `fleet.`, `thread.` or `testhook.` → `gate-fleet`;
  4. else `gate-core-domains`.

The explicit labels are POST /fleet/enrollments, POST /projects/:slug/vcs, PATCH /projects/:slug/vcs, POST /projects/:slug/vcs/webhook-secret/rotate, POST /projects/:slug/webhooks and PATCH /projects/:slug/webhooks/:id. Change AC-13's exact toHaveLength(12) to at least 12 so dependent gating stories can land individually; US-010 restores exact 41. Preserve sorted rollout-map equality and existing contract detection. Add parse-route-input unit cases and gate-secret cases in permission-contract.spec.ts.

**Scope** — In: parser, temporary feature union, explicit secret list, six relabels, rollout precedence and count lower bound. Out: registering/gating any domain route (US-002..US-009); removing gate-high or restoring exact 41 (US-010); gating secret-bearing routes.

**Interface** — `parseRouteInput(input, names)`; `SECRET_GATE_ROUTES: ReadonlySet<string>`; `PendingGateFeature` becomes `'gate-high' | 'gate-secret' | 'gate-core-domains' | 'gate-fleet'` in this story.

**Verification** — Three-session security TDD; pure parser/contract unit assertions plus booted-app rollout-map comparison using the shared DB gate and a host Postgres run.

userStories.title: Gate global and project budget writes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Gate the eight budget create, update, delete and resume HTTP routes through registered route commands.

**Motivation** — The 35 `gate-high` routes are the ones the design's shipped defaults already make agents wait on (`high` → `agent`), yet an agent calling them over REST or the `koda` CLI still writes at once: it can delete a project, a ticket or a runner, raise a budget or unregister a repo the moment it holds the key.

**Approach** — **One commands class per domain module, registered in that module.** The module imports `ApprovalEngineModule` (the registry and `ApprovalRouteGate`) and `AuthRepositoryModule` (`ActorPrincipalLoader`). `ApprovalEngineModule` imports nothing and is one instance per application, so importing it from many modules shares one registry.

Each row is one `routeCommand` registered by the story's commands class. "Scope" is the `projectId` passed to `ApprovalRouteGate.run` (`null` = global). The run calls the service the handler calls today, with `principal` the rebuilt `UserPrincipal | AgentPrincipal`. A route whose handler answers no body has a run that returns `null`, and its handler returns `undefined` on `executed` (204 or the route's status, as today). Every other run answers what the service answers, and the handler answers `JsonResponse.Ok(outcome.result)`. Every body-returning command declares `toResult: (result) => result`, so `ApprovalRequest.result` holds the body the route answers (the services already answer DTOs or plain objects); a no-body command declares no `toResult` and stores `null`.

Provide BudgetRouteCommands in BudgetsModule; BudgetRouteCommands.onModuleInit registers the eight BUDGET_ROUTE_VARIANTS:
| Route | Key | Scope | Variant | Input | Run |
| POST /fleet/budgets | fleet.budget.create | null | rest:fleet-budgets.create | parseBody(CreateBudgetPolicyDto, input) | budgets.create(principal.id, { kind: 'admin' }, dto) |
| PATCH /fleet/budgets/:id | fleet.budget.update | null | rest:fleet-budgets.update | { id, patch: parseBody(UpdateBudgetPolicyDto, …) } | budgets.update(principal.id, { kind: 'admin' }, id, patch) |
| DELETE /fleet/budgets/:id | fleet.budget.delete | null | rest:fleet-budgets.delete | { id } | budgets.remove(principal.id, { kind: 'admin' }, id) |
| POST /fleet/budgets/:id/resume | fleet.budget.resume | null | rest:fleet-budgets.resume | { id, body: parseBody(ResumeBudgetPolicyDto, …) } | budgets.resume(principal.id, { kind: 'admin' }, id, body.amountUsd) |
| POST /projects/:slug/fleet/budgets | fleet.budget.create | project | rest:project-fleet-budgets.create | { projectId, policy: parseBody(CreateBudgetPolicyDto, …) } | budgets.create(principal.id, { kind: 'project', projectId }, policy) |
| PATCH /projects/:slug/fleet/budgets/:id | fleet.budget.update | project | rest:project-fleet-budgets.update | { projectId, id, patch } | budgets.update(principal.id, { kind: 'project', projectId }, id, patch) |
| DELETE /projects/:slug/fleet/budgets/:id | fleet.budget.delete | project | rest:project-fleet-budgets.delete | { projectId, id } | budgets.remove(…, { kind: 'project', projectId }, id) |
| POST /projects/:slug/fleet/budgets/:id/resume | fleet.budget.resume | project | rest:project-fleet-budgets.resume | { projectId, id, body } | budgets.resume(…, { kind: 'project', projectId }, id, body.amountUsd) |

- The id members of every input are read with `parseRouteInput`. A body member is read with `parseBody` of the route's DTO; a missing body member is parsed as `{}`.

**The project id of a project route comes from `@CurrentProject()`.** `ProjectMembershipGuard` has already resolved it. Services that take a slug get the slug from the frozen input.

Inject ApprovalRouteGate into FleetBudgetsController and ProjectFleetBudgetsController. Each gated handler gains `@ApprovalGated()`, keeps its `@Requires` and `@ApiResponse`s, and throws ApprovalPending for pending. Keep route parameters declared, remove unused @Principal, retain existing executed statuses (create 201, update/resume 200, delete 204), and never freeze principal or config. Drop all eight budget PENDING_GATE_ROUTES rows in this story. Move service-call expectations from handler specs to budget-route.commands.spec.ts; handlers assert gate arguments and executed/pending mapping. Extend budgets.module.spec.ts to resolve BudgetRouteCommands with GlobalStubsModule.

**Scope** — In: one budget commands class, eight handlers, module wiring, allowlist removals and per-route behavior. Out: other fleet gates (US-003/US-004), shared parser/secret classification (US-001) and exact contract/OpenAPI closure (US-010). Do not pre-run service domain checks.

**Interface** — `BudgetsService.create/update/remove/resume(actorId, route: BudgetRoute, …)`, `BudgetRoute = { kind: 'admin' } | { kind: 'project'; projectId }`. Mirror `ApprovalRouteGate.run({ key, variant, projectId, input, keyCheck? })` and `routeCommand(spec, loader)` from 5a.

**Verification** — Three-session security TDD; commands/handler/DB-free module specs and real HTTP approval integration with fleet-budgets-api fixtures. Grant the four budget keys globally for global routes and with project.read in P for project routes; seed no policy. Approve using root POST /api/approvals/:id/decisions { decision: 'approve' }. Run DB specs outside sandbox.

AC-3 [integration]: PATCH /api/fleet/budgets/:id with { amountUsd: 42 } by the granted agent on a global policy returns 202; and When root approves that global update request, the policy's amountUsd is 42.

AC-6 [integration]: Given the budget keys and project.read in P, POST /api/projects/:slug/fleet/budgets with a valid project policy body by the agent returns { status: 202, data: { projectId: P } }; and When root approves that project create request, a project policy for P exists.

AC-15 [unit]: Given BudgetsModule compiled with GlobalStubsModule and no database, its container resolves BudgetRouteCommands.

userStories.title: Gate fleet repo, runner and analytics writes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Gate six fleet-admin REST writes using per-domain repo, runner and analytics command variants.

**Motivation** — Every other approvable write route is listed in `PENDING_GATE_ROUTES` with the feature that will gate it.

**Approach** — **One commands class per domain module, registered in that module.** The module imports `ApprovalEngineModule` (the registry and `ApprovalRouteGate`) and `AuthRepositoryModule` (`ActorPrincipalLoader`). `ApprovalEngineModule` imports nothing and is one instance per application, so importing it from many modules shares one registry.

Register FleetRepoRouteCommands/FLEET_REPO_ROUTE_VARIANTS in FleetReposModule, RunnerRouteCommands/RUNNER_ROUTE_VARIANTS in RunnersModule and AnalyticsRouteCommands/ANALYTICS_ROUTE_VARIANTS in AnalyticsModule. All six gate scopes are null, even when analytics filters a project.
| Route | Key | Variant | Input | Run |
| POST /fleet/repos | fleet.repo.create | rest:fleet-repos.create | parseBody(CreateFleetRepoDto, input) | repos.create(principal.id, dto) |
| DELETE /fleet/repos/:id | fleet.repo.delete | rest:fleet-repos.delete | { id } | repos.remove(principal.id, id) |
| POST /fleet/repos/:id/check | fleet.repo.check | rest:fleet-repos.check | { id } | repos.check(id) |
| PATCH /fleet/runners/:id | fleet.runner.update | rest:fleet-runners.update | { id, patch: parseBody(UpdateRunnerDto, …) } | runners.update(principal.id, id, patch) |
| DELETE /fleet/runners/:id | fleet.runner.delete | rest:fleet-runners.delete | { id } | runners.remove(principal.id, id) |
| DELETE /fleet/analytics | fleet.analytics.delete | rest:fleet-analytics.delete | { before, projectId?, confirm }: parseBody(DeleteAnalyticsQuery, { before, projectId }) merged with parseBody(DeleteAnalyticsBody, { confirm }) | analytics.deleteRows(principal.id, input, new Date()) |

- The id members of every input are read with `parseRouteInput`. A body member is read with `parseBody` of the route's DTO; a missing body member is parsed as `{}`.
- A missing or malformed `before` is refused with 400 by the global validation pipe before the handler runs, so no request opens; the handler passes `parseQuery(DeleteAnalyticsQuery, raw)` into the input as today. The run's `deleteRows` refuses a `confirm` that names neither the project's slug nor `ALL` (today's 400, now a `failed` request).

**Reads the handler already makes before its service call stay before the gate.** Their answers stay as today, and no request is opened when they refuse:
  - the analytics query validation (400 from the global validation pipe on `@Query() raw: DeleteAnalyticsQuery`; `parseQuery` only strips undeclared fields).
Every check inside a service runs when the command runs, at once or after approval; a failing check settles the request `failed`. This is 5a's rule.

Inject ApprovalRouteGate into FleetReposController, RunnersController and FleetAnalyticsController; decorate only these six handlers @ApprovalGated(), preserve Requires/guards/ApiResponses/path parameters, and map pending to ApprovalPending. Body-returning commands use identity toResult and JsonResponse.Ok(outcome.result); no-body repo/runner deletion commands return null without toResult and handlers return undefined preserving 204. Pass a new Date when analytics executes, not when requesting. Drop six matching allowlist rows. Update affected controller specs to gate assertions and move service expectations to the three new command specs.

**Scope** — In: three commands classes/modules, six handlers and their allowlist removals. Out: budget/schedule gates (US-002/US-004), shared parser (US-001), exact route count/OpenAPI (US-010), real forge checks in tests and enrollment's secret-bearing route.

**Interface** — `FleetReposService.create(actorId, dto)`, `.remove(actorId, id)`, `.check(id, now?)`; `RunnersService.update(actorId, id, dto)`, `.remove(actorId, id)`; `AnalyticsService.deleteRows(actorId, q: DeleteInput, now)`.

**Verification** — Three-session security TDD; command registration/parser and handler unit cases, then gated-fleet-admin-routes HTTP integration with global grants and real root decisions. Stub forge checks as fleet-repos.integration.spec.ts does; use fleet-analytics-delete.integration.spec.ts data fixtures. Assert no mutation before approval and failed outcomes on service refusal; DB tests must execute outside sandbox.

AC-2 [integration]: When root approves that request and the stubbed forge check passes, the repo is registered; and When root approves that successful repo-create request, it settles executed.

AC-3 [integration]: An approved repo create whose forge check fails when the command runs settles failed with result matching { error: 'execution-failed', name: forgeFailure.name }, where forgeFailure is the Error rejected by the forge-check stub; and When the approved repo create's forge check fails, no repo is registered.

userStories.title: Gate schedule deletion and repo drift checks
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Gate schedule deletion and repo drift submission while re-evaluating schedule administration at execution time.

**Motivation** — The 35 `gate-high` routes are the ones the design's shipped defaults already make agents wait on (`high` → `agent`), yet an agent calling them over REST or the `koda` CLI still writes at once: it can delete a project, a ticket or a runner, raise a budget or unregister a repo the moment it holds the key.

**Approach** — **One commands class per domain module, registered in that module.** The module imports `ApprovalEngineModule` (the registry and `ApprovalRouteGate`) and `AuthRepositoryModule` (`ActorPrincipalLoader`). `ApprovalEngineModule` imports nothing and is one instance per application, so importing it from many modules shares one registry.

**The project id of a project route comes from `@CurrentProject()`.** `ProjectMembershipGuard` has already resolved it. Services that take a slug get the slug from the frozen input.

**The gate key is the route's `@Requires` key.** For an ownable key (`comment.delete`, `ticket.link.remove`, `kb.document.delete`, `fleet.schedule.delete`), `ApprovalRouteGate` already accepts `<key>.own`. The row-level check (whose row it is) runs in the command.

**The schedule command recomputes "may administer" when it runs:** `(await permissions.can(principal, 'fleet.schedule.delete', { projectId })).allowed`, the controller's `canAdminister` rule. A deferred delete is judged on the principal's keys at execution.

| Route | Key | Scope | Variant | Input | Run |
| DELETE /projects/:slug/fleet/schedules/:id | fleet.schedule.delete | project | rest:project-fleet-schedules.delete | { projectId, id } | schedules.remove(principal.id, projectId, id, canAdminister), canAdminister computed as above |
| POST /projects/:slug/fleet/repos/:repoId/drift-checks | fleet.repo.drift.check | project | rest:project-repo-config.drift-check | { projectId, repoId } | configJobs.submitDrift(principal.id, projectId, repoId) |

Add ScheduleRouteCommands/SCHEDULE_ROUTE_VARIANTS in SchedulesModule and RepoConfigRouteCommands/REPO_CONFIG_ROUTE_VARIANTS in RepoConfigModule. Use parseRouteInput for all identifiers; register in onModuleInit via routeCommand and ActorPrincipalLoader. Inject ApprovalRouteGate into ProjectFleetSchedulesController and ProjectRepoConfigController; only remove/submitDrift are gated. Move the remove handler's canAdminister call into its command, not into frozen input; preserve other controller helper uses. Add @ApprovalGated(), retain Requires, guards, response metadata and path parameters, and throw ApprovalPending on pending. Schedule run returns null, omits toResult and handler returns undefined preserving 204; drift command uses identity toResult and handler JsonResponse.Ok(outcome.result), preserving 201 on immediate execution. Remove the two corresponding allowlist rows.

Update enforce-fleet-config-knowledge.integration.spec.ts: its AC-7 (a DEVELOPER agent queues a drift check, 201) now expects 202 with data.permissionKey fleet.repo.drift.check; its AC-8 approves that request as root, then asserts the created CONFIG_DRIFT job has requestedById the agent and requestedByType AGENT. Extend schedules.module.spec.ts to resolve ScheduleRouteCommands. Move handler service expectations to command unit specs.

**Scope** — In: these two route commands, two module imports/providers, two handlers, current-key ownership semantics and their allowlist rows. Out: other schedule mutations and config-edit routes; shared parser/classification (US-001); budget/fleet-admin gates (US-002/US-003); exact count/OpenAPI closure (US-010).

**Interface** — `SchedulesService.remove(actorId, projectId, id, canAdminister)`; `ConfigJobsService.submitDrift(actorId, projectId, repoId)`.

**Verification** — Three-session security TDD with .own/all-row schedule cases, registration and DB-free module resolution, plus real HTTP root approvals in gated-project-fleet-routes.integration.spec.ts. Use fleet-schedules-api and fleet-repo-config-api fixtures, project.read grants and no seeded policy. Preserve the member-human 201 drift regression and agent job attribution; run DB integration outside sandbox.

AC-3 [integration]: DELETE /api/projects/:slug/fleet/schedules/:id by an agent holding only fleet.schedule.delete.own plus project.read in P on another user's schedule returns 202; and When root approves that other-owner schedule-delete request, it settles failed; and When that .own deletion fails, the other user's schedule remains.

| DELETE /agents/:slug | agent.delete | null | rest:agents.delete | { slug } | agents.remove(slug) |
| DELETE /admin/skills/sources/:id | skill.source.delete | null | rest:admin-skill-sources.delete | { id } | skills.deleteSource(id) |

Project/skill-source delete commands return null with no toResult, and executed handlers return undefined preserving 204. Agent deletion remains hard delete with service result, identity toResult and JsonResponse.Ok(outcome.result), preserving 200. Remove these three allowlist rows.

userStories.title: Extract and gate KB document deletion
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extract KB deletion into a rechecking service and gate the document-delete HTTP route without losing its immediate preflight refusals.

**Motivation** — Every other approvable write route is listed in `PENDING_GATE_ROUTES` with the feature that will gate it.

**Approach** — **KB deletion moves into a service.** The handler's preflight, delete loop and audit move to `KbDocumentDeletion` (rag module) unchanged:
  - `preflight(principal, projectId, sourceId, source?)` answers the creators by source after the ownership check;
  - `delete(principal, projectId, sourceId, source?)` runs `preflight` again, then deletes and audits as today.

The handler calls `preflight` before the gate so a refusal is immediate; the command calls `delete`, so a deferred run re-checks ownership.

**`RagController`'s own helpers stay.** `assertMayDeleteRow` and `mayDeleteAnyRow` are also used by `addDocument` and stay in the controller; `KbDocumentDeletion` makes its own `PermissionService.can` check.

- The KB handler: `resolveProject(slug)` (404 `rag`), `kbDeletion.preflight(principal, project.id, sourceId, query.source)`, then the gate.

| Route | Key | Scope | Variant | Input | Run |
| DELETE /projects/:slug/kb/documents/:sourceId | kb.document.delete | project | rest:kb-documents.delete | { projectId, sourceId, source? } (source validated by DeleteKbDocumentQuery) | kbDeletion.delete(principal, projectId, sourceId, source), answering { deleted: true } |

**One commands class per domain module, registered in that module.** The module imports `ApprovalEngineModule` (the registry and `ApprovalRouteGate`) and `AuthRepositoryModule` (`ActorPrincipalLoader`). `ApprovalEngineModule` imports nothing and is one instance per application, so importing it from many modules shares one registry.

Provide KbDocumentDeletion and KbRouteCommands/KB_ROUTE_VARIANTS in RagModule; register routeCommand in onModuleInit with ActorPrincipalLoader. Parse projectId/sourceId using parseRouteInput, optional source using parseBody(DeleteKbDocumentQuery, …), and reject source web with approvals.invalidInput. Omitted source retains both KB_DELETE_SOURCES (doc/manual), never ticket/code. KbDocumentDeletion.preflight reads every chosen source's creators and checks permissions.can(principal, 'kb.document.delete', { projectId, resource: { createdBy } }) for every creator before any deletion; delete redoes the full preflight, then deletes each chosen source and audits only sources with matching rows. Preserve current filter-safe-id validation. The command returns { deleted: true } with toResult: (result) => result.

Inject KbDocumentDeletion and ApprovalRouteGate into RagController. deleteDocument keeps @Principal(), all path params, Requires/guards/ApiResponses, adds @ApprovalGated(), performs resolveProject/preflight/gate in that order, throws ApprovalPending for pending and returns JsonResponse.Ok(outcome.result) on executed preserving 200. Remove only its allowlist row.

Move controller ownership/source/audit specs to kb-document-deletion.service.spec.ts; keep handler preflight and gate-call/pending/executed cases in rag.controller.spec.ts. Provide both doubles in kb-documents-membership.routes.spec.ts, graphify-kb-validation.integration.spec.ts and rag-api-project-id-validation.integration.spec.ts without assertion changes. In project-membership.guard.routes.spec.ts add KbDocumentDeletion.preflight resolving [] beside US-005's existing gate double; keep the KB DELETE refusal 403 and no deleteBySource assertion.

**Scope** — In: extraction with unchanged preflight/loop/audit behavior, execution-time ownership recheck, one gate/command and module/fixture wiring. Out: changing addDocument or its helpers, deleting ticket/code sources, other project/ticket gates (US-005/US-007), shared parsing (US-001) and exact contract/OpenAPI closure (US-010).

**Interface** — `preflight(principal, projectId, sourceId, source?)`; `delete(principal, projectId, sourceId, source?)`; `RagService.findSourceCreators(projectId, source, sourceId)`, `.deleteBySource(projectId, source, sourceId)`; `KB_DELETE_SOURCES`; `PermissionService.can`.

**Verification** — Three-session security TDD.
